topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides introductory framing for the lecture, acknowledging the complexity of complement and framing expectations for the session.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the complement system and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture, nomenclature, and central activation mechanism of the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three recognition pathways that detect pathogens and generate surface-bound convertases to reach the complement activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream mechanisms through which activated complement destroys pathogens and promotes immune clearance.

topics.label: Regulation of complement on host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent the complement cascade from destroying healthy host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical presentations and disease susceptibilities associated with deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies used by pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, to circumvent complement-mediated clearance.

topics.label: Closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and provides a transition to the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
